```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`streamConnect` connects data stream sources and stream mining algorithms
through sockets or web services. It works with the `DSD` (data stream) and
`DSC` (data stream clustering) interfaces from the [stream package](https://github.com/mhahsler/stream).

This guide shows two common workflows: reading a stream over a socket and
updating a remote clusterer through a web service. For more control over the
web service endpoints and deployment, see the help pages for
`publish_DSD_via_WebService()` and `publish_DSC_via_WebService()`.

## Install and load

Install the released package from CRAN:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("streamConnect")
```

Load the package and select an available local port for the examples:

```{r load}
library(streamConnect)
```

We will use the same free server port throughout this vignette. Some systems do
not allow the use of local ports, then the code in this vignette will not be
executed.

```{r find-socket}
run_code <- TRUE
tryCatch({
  port <- httpuv::randomPort()

  }, warning = function(w) {
    message("Ports unavailable: ", w)
    run_code <<- FALSE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Ports unavailable: ", e)
    run_code <<- FALSE
})
```


## Read a data stream over a socket

Start a background process that publishes a stream. The publisher opens a
socket server and writes data in blocks. Since the socket format does not
include column names, provide them when creating the reader.

```{r socket-publish, eval=run_code}
socket_process <- publish_DSD_via_Socket(
  DSD_Gaussians(k = 3, d = 2),
  port = port
)
socket_process
```

Connect a local `DSD` reader and request points from the stream:

```{r socket-read, eval=run_code}
socket_dsd <- DSD_ReadSocket(
  port = port,
  col.names = c("x", "y", ".class")
)

points <- get_points(socket_dsd, n = 10)
head(points)
```

Close the reader and stop the publisher when finished:

```{r socket-stop, eval=run_code}
close_stream(socket_dsd)
if (socket_process$is_alive()) socket_process$kill()
```

## Update a remote clusterer via a web service

Web services also support request and response operations. Start a clusterer
in a background process, then create a local `DSC` interface for it:

```{r webservice-start, eval=run_code}
clusterer_process <- publish_DSC_via_WebService(
  "DSC_DBSTREAM(r = .05)",
  port = port
)

clusterer <- DSC_WebService(paste0("http://127.0.0.1:", port))
clusterer
```

Send a batch of points to the remote clusterer and retrieve its centers and
weights through the local interface:

```{r webservice-update, eval=run_code}
stream <- DSD_Gaussians(k = 3, d = 2, noise = 0.05)
update(clusterer, stream, n = 500)

get_centers(clusterer)
get_weights(clusterer)
```

Stop the service process when the work is complete:

```{r webservice-stop, eval=run_code}
if (clusterer_process$is_alive()) clusterer_process$kill()
```

## Publish a stream through a web service

To expose a data source over HTTP, publish a `DSD` and read it with
`DSD_ReadWebService()`. The service returns CSV by default; JSON and RDS
serialization are also available through the `serializer` argument.

```{r webservice-stream, eval=run_code}
source_process <- publish_DSD_via_WebService(
  "DSD_Gaussians(k = 3, d = 2)",
  port = port
)

remote_stream <- DSD_ReadWebService(paste0("http://127.0.0.1:", port))
get_points(remote_stream, n = 10)
```

```{r webservice-stream2, eval=run_code}
if (source_process$is_alive()) source_process$kill()
```

## Next steps

- Use `publish_DSD_via_Socket()` and `DSD_ReadSocket()` for continuous
  point-to-point stream transfer.
- Use `publish_DSD_via_WebService()` and `DSD_ReadWebService()` to serve
  stream data over HTTP.
- Use `publish_DSC_via_WebService()` and `DSC_WebService()` to update and
  inspect a remote clusterer.
- Set `serve = FALSE` to write a plumber task file for deployment with a
  hosting environment of your choice.

See the [package reference](https://michael.hahsler.net/streamConnect/reference/)
for the full function documentation.
